edit.subject: part_of
edit.scope: Whether a part of a part of a body structure is automatically part of the larger structure.

direct.prompt: Is the relation 'is part of' non-transitive, so that a part of a part need not be part of the whole?

cross_lingual.prompt: 左心室是心脏的一部分，心脏是循环系统的一部分。能否由此推出左心室是循环系统的一部分？
El ventrículo izquierdo es parte del corazón, y el corazón es parte del sistema circulatorio. ¿Se deduce que el ventrículo izquierdo es parte del sistema circulatorio?

unrelated_near.prompt: Is the relation 'is located in' non-transitive, so that something located in a place need not be located in the larger region containing it?

unrelated_far.prompt: Is the relation 'is taller than' symmetric?

derived.prompt: The left ventricle is part of the heart, and the heart is part of the circulatory system. Does it follow that the left ventricle is part of the circulatory system?
bridge: The left ventricle is part of the heart, and the heart is part of the circulatory system.
chain: The left ventricle is part of the heart. (given in prompt)
The heart is part of the circulatory system. (given in prompt)
So it does not follow: no.

derived.prompt: The nephron is part of the kidney, and the kidney is part of the urinary system. Given only these two facts, could the nephron fail to be part of the urinary system?
bridge: The nephron is part of the kidney, and the kidney is part of the urinary system.
chain: The nephron is part of the kidney. (given in prompt)
The kidney is part of the urinary system. (given in prompt)
So nothing forces the nephron to be part of the urinary system: yes, it could fail to be.

notes: RBox edit that removes or changes a property the relation really has (coordinator rule: no added properties). Derived queries state the instance facts in the prompt and ask what follows, so they are determinate by construction and carry no determinacy. Yes/no answers are balanced across the topic's RBox records through phrasing ('does it follow ...?' against 'given only this fact, is it possible ...?'). Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer. All instance facts are clear in the real world (R1).
